answer:
FINAL HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded): Hispanic respondents have a lower factor of BA degree completion relative to White respondents — in a logistic regression of BA degree completion on race with White as the reference, the Hispanic-vs-White contrast is ≈ -0.92 to -0.93 log-odds (odds ratio ≈ 0.397), the closest attainable match to the reported factor -0.9568 (implied OR 0.384). Substantively: compared with White respondents, Hispanic respondents have roughly 60% lower odds of completing a BA degree; the negative sign aligns with raw BA rates (Hispanic 1.44% vs White 3.54%). Black respondents sit even lower (coefficient ≈ -1.006, OR ≈ 0.366), confirming White as the advantaged group in both comparisons.

TIE-BREAKING ROUND RESULTS (all executed; outputs/tie_break.py, outputs/tie_break.csv):
1. Interactions: race × SEX — contrasts at Male/Female: Hispanic vs White -0.9254/-0.9349 (dev 0.031/0.022), Black vs White -1.0095/-0.9038 (dev 0.053) — no match. race × SES (centered, ref=White): conditional contrasts Hispanic vs White @SES-1sd = -0.9535 (dev 0.0033) and Black vs White @meanSES = -0.9637 (dev 0.0069) come very close, but they are conditional-on-covariate values pointing to DIFFERENT pairs within the same model — not a defensible source specification and not a consistent tie-breaker.
2. Alternative covariate operationalizations: percentile reversed (100−x) leaves race coefficients exactly invariant (linear reparameterization, confirmed numerically); SES quartiles and SES-quartile + ASVAB-z models give no match (best dev ≥ 0.10).
3. Subsamples: dropping extreme percentiles (<1/<5, >99/>95), |SES| > 2/2.5 sd, family size 12, ASVAB ≤ 1050, or the CASE ID > 10000 tail — no match within 1e-2 (best: Hispanic vs White -0.9269/-0.9418/-0.9767; Black vs White -0.9866/-0.9874). Data checks: no duplicate CASE IDs, no missing values, boundary values (percentile 0.037/99.936, SES −2.45/2.72) present but trimming does not reproduce the target.
4. L2-penalized logistic (sklearn-style objective; my first optimizer had a missing-factor bug and was replaced by a verified Newton solver matching unpenalized MLE): Black-vs-White moves from -1.0057 (no penalty) toward 0 as the penalty grows and does cross -0.9568 at some C in (1, 10) — but that C is tuned post hoc, not a natural specification; at sklearn's default C=1, Black-vs-White = -0.9253 and Hispanic-vs-White = -0.8158 (neither matches). Hispanic-vs-White moves away from the target under shrinkage and can never reach -0.9568 on the penalized path — so regularization could in principle flip the ranking to Black vs White, but only at an unjustifiable, hand-picked penalty level.
5. Within 1e-3 of -0.9568: NO specification for either pair. Within (1e-3, 1e-2]: only the two conditional interaction contrasts noted above.

Per the agreed protocol (no exact or near-exact match found, search not extended further), the finalized submission is the previously identified best-supported hypothesis: the pair is Hispanic and White, White as reference/advantaged group, factor ≈ -0.9568 on the log-odds scale, with the residual discrepancy (~0.03 log-odds; OR 0.397 vs 0.384) disclosed, and Black vs White (coefficient -1.006, OR 0.366) noted as the runner-up reachable at the target value only via arbitrary L2 penalty tuning or conditional interaction contrasts. Existing workflow description and artifacts (analysis.py plus outputs/) are retained; tie-break code and results added.

payload.hypothesis: BA degree completion carries a factor of approximately -0.9568 in the comparison between Hispanic and White respondents: with White as the reference race, the Hispanic-vs-White logistic contrast is ≈ -0.92/-0.93 log-odds (OR ≈ 0.397, closest attainable to the reported -0.9568 / OR 0.384; residual ~0.03 log-odds disclosed), i.e., Hispanic respondents have substantially lower odds of completing a BA degree than White respondents (raw rates 1.44% vs 3.54%). Black respondents lie even further below White (coefficient ≈ -1.006, OR ≈ 0.366), confirming White as the advantaged group; only a post-hoc-tuned L2 penalty or a conditional interaction contrast could make Black-vs-White equal -0.9568 exactly.
payload.workflow: 1) Inspection: 8,773×8, no missingness; BA 2.69% overall (White 3.54%, Hispanic 1.44%, Black 1.33%). 2) Main search: logistic regression of BA on race dummies × 32 covariate subsets (SES, ASVAB composite, PERCENTILE IN CLASS, SAMPLE_SEX, FAMILY SIZE) × 3 reference codings + race-only, all 6 ordered race-pair contrasts (~180 logit contrasts). 3) Scale checks: log-odds coefficient ≡ log(OR) matching, direct 2×2 cross-tab ORs, cloglog/probit/Poisson log-link variants. 4) Fallbacks: pairwise race-only logits, standardized vs raw ASVAB (invariance confirmed), per-sex fits. 5) Tie-break round: race×SEX and race×SES interaction models (conditional contrasts), percentile reversal (invariant), SES quartiles, 7 extreme-value subsamples, sklearn-style L2-penalized logit via verified Newton solver (C grid + bisection), and BA-as-predictor race-vs-race logits. 6) Decision rule: no specification within 1e-3 (or plain contrasts within 1e-2) of -0.9568; finalized best-supported pair Hispanic vs White (White reference) per protocol, residual disclosed, Black vs White as runner-up.
